title: Path-based Explanation for Knowledge Graph Completion

problem.claim: GNN-based knowledge graph completion models predict facts, but their explanations have not received sufficient attention.

gap.claim: Path-based explanation methods for knowledge graphs, particularly for GNN-based KGC models, have not been well explored.

contributions.claim: Power-Link is a path-based explainer for GNN-based knowledge graph completion models.
The method uses a simplified graph-powering technique with fully parallelisable and memory-efficient training.
The authors introduce three quantitative explanation metrics and a qualitative human evaluation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Power-Link as the first path-based KGC explainer that explores GNN-based models and describe the graph-powering technique as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments reportedly show that Power-Link outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in interpretability, efficiency, and scalability.
The implementation is reported to be publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs have achieved success in knowledge graph completion by modelling entity-relation interactions.
Explanations for predicted facts have received insufficient attention, despite their value for transparency and model reliability.
Existing explanation practices are instance- or subgraph-based, while path-based explanation methods remain underexplored.
Power-Link addresses the gap with path-based explanations, a graph-powering technique, and new evaluation measures.
The authors report superior interpretability, efficiency, and scalability compared with state-of-the-art baselines.

source_observation.claim: Paths may provide more user-friendly and interpretable explanations than instance- or subgraph-based explanations in some scenarios.

interpretation.claim: Explanation structure should be selected according to the needs of the explanation scenario rather than treated as universally interchangeable.

application.claim: When designing explanations for graph predictions, evaluate path-based representations alongside instance- or subgraph-based alternatives.

exception.claim: The abstract limits the advantage of paths to some scenarios and does not establish that they are preferable in all settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, experimental settings, or numerical results.
The abstract does not define the three evaluation metrics or describe the human evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or establish independent verification of the reported results.
